The name Gensho carries the meaning “God's Treasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Japanese tradition and is also used in Japanese. Parents who choose Gensho usually hope their child will grow to embody god's treasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Gensho carries a deep spiritual significance, reminding us of the inner wisdom and knowledge that comes from a higher power. It inspires us to seek out self-reflection, meditation, and prayer in order to tap into this divine treasure and find peace, happiness, and enlightenment. historical_references.reference: Gensho was a famous Japanese monk who visited India in 1223 CE to study Buddhism under the tutelage of Jianantara and Jatiprajnana. He later became a key figure in the spread of the Tendai school of Buddhism in Japan.
historical_references.context: Japanese monk's pilgrimage to India to study Buddhism

historical_references.reference: Gensho (玄奘) was also a renowned Chinese poet and calligrapher of the Sui Dynasty. He is famous for his poems on the subjects of the moon, mountains, and other natural wonders, which continue to be widely studied and appreciated in China and Japan.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Gensho' has found modern usage in the context of Buddhism and Zen meditation. It is often used as a term for a deep, profound awakening or enlightenment experience. Gensho is seen on several platforms including the internet, where it is a popular search term for those seeking information on Zen meditation and enlightenment experiences. It is also seen on smartphone apps, where various Zen meditation apps offer guided sessions and resources to help users achieve a gensho experience. Lastly, retreat centers that offer Zen meditation and mindfulness training also use the term to describe the transformative experiences that participants may encounter during their stays.
